the photon scattering cross sections of heavy nuclei are very well described by the Lorentzian model down to about 10–20% of the giant dipole resonance energy, and that the photon strength is well described by the same model down to about half the neutron separation energy.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the question how well the giant dipole resonance strength can be described by a superposition of Lorentzians, which is the basis of the standard method of extracting the dipole strength from photon scattering and average neutron capture data.
a detailed study of the electric dipolar response of nuclei.
the question how far the giant resonance is a unique phenomenon in the energy spectrum of the electric diprole strength in nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the giant dipole resonance is a well‐defined and universal feature of the nuclear structure, and that the Lorentzian model gives an excellent description of the energy dependence of the dipole strength in all nuclei, provided the proper deformation effects are included in the model.
the Lorentzian model gives a good description of photon strength distributions in heavy nuclei, provided that the parameters are adjusted to photo‐nuclear data.
for the energy region of the giant dipole resonance, the photon strength distribution can be described by Lorentzians, with the parameters obtained from the neutron data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the giant dipole resonance in heavy nuclei is a well‐defined resonance with a width which is determined mainly by the average spacing of neutron resonances.
the energy dependence of the giant dipole strength is well represented by a Lorentzian with a width of about 3 MeV and a centroid energy of about 12.5 A−1/3 MeV.
the energy dependence of the photon strength function is not a unique function but depends on the energy region considered, the type of transition, and the nuclear structure of the nucleus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Lorentzian description of the dipole strength in the region between the giant dipole and the neutron threshold works well.
the photon strength is very well represented by a sum of Lorentzians down to the lowest excitation energies.
the electric dipole response of heavy nuclei is well described by a Lorentzian distribution with an energy width of the order of 2 MeV.
